title: Protocol for isolation and spectral flow cytometry analysis of immune cells from the murine exocrine and endocrine pancreas
protocol: Euthanize mice.
Perfuse the pancreas with a collagenase solution immediately after euthanasia.
Excise the pancreas.
Incubate tubes containing perfused pancreata in a 37°C water bath for half an hour.
Filtrate to separate islets from the exocrine pancreas.
Insert 30 G needle into the musculus sphincter of Oddi.
Inject collagenase solution into the common bile duct.
Perfuse the pancreas with collagenase type IV solution.
Add 2 mL of collagenase solution to a 50 mL conical tube and keep on ice.
Euthanize the mouse.
Incubate the perfused pancreas in a water bath for 30 min.
Run the digested sample through a 500 μm strainer.
Filter unfiltered leftovers from the top of the strainer into a well-perfused pancreas container.
Transfer exocrine tissue through a 70 μm inverted strainer, leaving islets behind.
Submerge strainer in a tissue culture dish with 5 mL of media to liberate islets.
Filter exocrine tissue through a 40 μm strainer and place the filtrate in a 50 mL falcon tube.
Spray the mouse with 70% ethanol.
Make a V-shape cut at the abdomen to open the mouse.
Subtract the skin coat by hand.
Open the peritoneum with scissors.
Reveal and cut the heart apex (ventricle) to drain blood.
Soak all blood with tissue paper.
Use a thread to make a knot surrounding the common bile duct near the liver.
Free the common bile duct using pointed forceps.
Clamp the duodenum on the right side of the musculus sphincter of Oddi.
Inject 2 mL collagenase solution into the musculus sphincter of Oddi.
Remove the omentum located between the spleen and stomach.
Separate the pancreas from the stomach and gut.
Remove the spleen from the pancreas.
Place the isolated pancreas in a 50 mL conical tube containing 2 mL of collagenase solution.
Put the tube on ice if multiple pancreata are being processed simultaneously.
Perfuse the pancreas, even for exocrine tissue use only.
Ensure the 30 G needle is inserted into the pancreatic duct via the musculus sphincter of Oddi.
Incubate the perfused pancreas in a 37°C water bath without shaking for 30 minutes.
Shake the falcon tube 30–40 times to create a homogenous solution after incubation.
Add ice-cold quenching buffer (QB) to stop the action of the collagenase and invert the tube 3 times before centrifuging at 570 g, 2 min, 4°C.
Wash tissue with QB, aspirate the QB, but leave the pellet.
Add 35 mL QB, briefly vortex three times and spin down at 570 g, 2 min, 4°C.

Pass the mixture through a 500 μm strainer into a new 50 mL conical tube after aspiration of supernatant and addition of 10 mL QB with pipetting up and down five times using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Wash the initial tube with an additional 10 mL QB to collect the remaining islets and run it through the 500 μm strainer as well.
Prepare a 15 cm dish with a spacer and put a 70 μm strainer on top of the spacer.
Pass the mixture through a 70 μm strainer into another conical tube to separate islets and exocrine pancreas.
Run the solution containing the islets from the 50 mL falcon tube through the inverted 70 μm strainer.
Wash the remaining islets with an additional 10 mL QB and run it through the 70 μm strainer.
Transfer the islets from the strainer into a 6 cm tissue culture dish containing 5 mL of islet culture media by inverting the strainer and dipping it in the media.
Liberate remaining islets potentially stuck to the bottom of the filter using a pipette tip moved across the top of the filter.
Put the islets in the dish into a cell culture incubator for at least 15 minutes to recover from isolation.
Filter the exocrine tissue, previously filtered through the 70 μm strainer, again through a 40 μm strainer directly into a new falcon tube.
Pellet the exocrine tissue by centrifuging at 350 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Hand-pick islets before dispersing them with trypsin.
Enrich immune cells from exocrine tissue by density centrifugation using Percoll.
Prepare stock Percoll: Mix 90% pure Percoll with 10% 10x PBS.
Create 70% Percoll: Combine 70% stock Percoll with 30% 1x PBS.
Create 40% Percoll: Blend 40% stock Percoll with 60% 1x PBS.
Pipette 4 ml of 40% Percoll into a 15 ml tube.
Add a glass pipette to the 15 ml tube containing 40% Percoll.
After centrifugation of the exocrine tissue, aspirate supernatant and resuspend pellet in 1 mL 70% Percoll using a 1000 μL pipette.
Add an additional 3 mL of 70% Percoll and mix.
Fill the glass pipette with the resuspended cells containing 70%/40% Percoll gradient.
Centrifuge: 20 min, 600 g, 22°C, with minimal brake and acceleration.
Prepare 10 mL flow cytometry staining buffer in a 15 mL tube.
Aspirate the first layer containing fat and debris and discard it.
Take 3-4 mL from the ring layer (lymphocytes) and transfer to the 15 mL tube containing 10 mL FB buffer.
Spin down: 250 g, 5 min, 4°C.
Hand-pick islets under a stereo microscope using a 10 μL pipette.
Transfer the picked islets into a new tissue culture dish containing 5 mL of islet culture media.
Repick islets from the tissue culture dish into a 15 mL tube containing 10 mL PBS.
Spin down the tube at 350 g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant using a pipette.
Add 800 μL of dissociation buffer to the tube.
Add 200 μL of 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA (1x) solution to achieve an end concentration of 0.01% Trypsin.
Put the tube in a 37°C water bath.
Pipette up and down three times with a 1000 μL pipette every 30 seconds for up to one minute and thirty seconds, avoiding foaming.
Observe islet dissociation progress.
After one minute and thirty seconds, reduce trypsin activity by adding 10 mL of ice-cold PBS.
Keep the cells on ice.
Spin down the tube at 250 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Wash cells twice with PBS before staining the cells to avoid the presence of proteins in the staining buffer.
Vortex beads for 30 seconds and add one drop of beads into 200 μL of FB (beads solution).
Aliquot 50 μL of beads solution into 5 mL flow cytometry tubes.
Add one μL of each antibody into 50 μL beads solution in the flow cytometry tube.
Vortex flow cytometry tubes.
Incubate for 20 minutes on ice in the dark.
Add 200 μL FB and mix the beads.
Spin down the mixture at 600 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the beads in 200 μL of FB.
Spin down the mixture at 600 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the beads in 200 μL of FB.
Pass cells through a 5 mL flow cytometry tube with a 35 μm strainer.
Wash cells twice with PBS.
If trypsin activity is reduced with PBS, one wash is sufficient.
Take a 20 μL sample for cell counting.
Count the cells using a cell counter to determine the total number of cells per sample.
Add 50 μL of PBS containing 1:2000 Zombie NIR to the pellet and pipette up and down.
Incubate in the dark at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Add 150 μL of PBS and resuspend the cells.
Spin down the mixture at 250 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Add DAPI (1.38 μg/mL) immediately before acquiring samples.
Stain cells with CD16/CD32 antibody by adding 50 μL of blocking solution containing the antibody for 10 min on ice in the dark.
Add 50 μl antibody mix directly to the sample after CD16/CD32 staining.
Stain for 20 min on ice in the dark.
Add 100 μL of fixation buffer and pipette up and down.
Spin down at 250 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Wash cells once with 200 μL of fixation buffer.
Resuspend the cells in 200 μL of fixation buffer.
Filter through flow cytometry tubes with a 35 μm strainer cap before acquiring samples.
Acquire the samples using a Cytek Aurora.
Keep samples on ice throughout the process.
Analyze the samples with FlowJo or another suitable software package.
